title: B2 · L4 — wish / if only (past)
topic: Expressing past regrets with wish + past perfect
description: 'Wish' y 'if only' + past perfect para expresar arrepentimientos sobre el pasado. Uno de los recursos más importantes para la reflexión personal en B2.

questions.prompt: Situación: enviaste un email en caliente ayer y ahora te arrepientes.
questions.question: Complete: 'I wish I ___ that email yesterday.'
options: didn't send
hadn't sent
wouldn't send
haven't sent
questions.explanation: 'Wish + past perfect' expresa arrepentimiento por una acción pasada YA CONSUMADA. La forma 'hadn't sent' equivale al español 'ojalá no lo hubiera enviado'. Error típico: usar past simple ('I wish I didn't send'), que sonaría a rutina pasada, no a arrepentimiento puntual.
examples: God, I wish I hadn't said that in the meeting — she looked hurt. → arrepentimiento inmediato
I really wish I hadn't quit my job on impulse last month.

questions.prompt: Un colega te cuenta sobre una oferta laboral que rechazó.
questions.question: Which sentence expresses regret about a past decision?
options: I wish I take that job.
I wish I took that job.
I wish I had taken that job.
I wish I will take that job.
questions.explanation: 'Wish + had + participio' es la fórmula fija para arrepentimientos pasados: la acción ya sucedió (o no sucedió) y no puede deshacerse. La opción B ('took') sería para un deseo presente. Recuerda: cuanto más 'atrás' el verbo (past → past perfect), más 'atrás' en el tiempo el arrepentimiento.
examples: I wish I had accepted that startup offer — they IPO'd last year. → reflexión profesional
Honestly, I wish I had listened to my mum when she said not to marry him.

questions.statement: 'I wish I had studied more' significa que la persona estudió mucho.
questions.explanation: FALSO — significa exactamente lo CONTRARIO. La estructura 'wish + had + PP' siempre invierte la realidad: si digo 'I wish I had studied', la realidad es que NO estudié lo suficiente y ahora lo lamento. Truco mnemotécnico: 'wish' es una máquina que le da la vuelta al hecho real.
examples: I wish I had studied harder for the finals. → realidad: no estudié bastante y suspendí
I wish I had saved more in my 20s. → realidad: gasté todo y ahora no tengo colchón

questions.text: I wish I had booked the tickets earlier. Now they're twice the price.
questions.explanation: Connected speech: 'I had' se contrae naturalmente a 'I'd' /aɪd/ en hablado rápido, aunque aquí la dictación se dicta completa para claridad. 'Twice the' se fusiona con la /s/ enlazada: 'twice-ðə'. La segunda frase suele añadirse en habla natural para justificar el lamento con la consecuencia actual.
examples: I wish I'd reserved a table at that Italian place — there's a two-hour wait now.
I wish I'd left home earlier. This traffic is a nightmare. → queja al llegar tarde

questions.prompt: Reflexionas sobre un amigo con quien perdiste contacto.
questions.question: Complete: 'If only I ___ him when I had the chance.'
options: called
had called
would call
have called
questions.explanation: 'If only + past perfect' expresa arrepentimiento pasado con más intensidad emocional que 'I wish'. La estructura es idéntica pero el tono es más lamentoso, casi poético. Se usa mucho cuando hablamos de oportunidades perdidas o palabras no dichas.
examples: If only I had told her how I felt before she moved to Australia. → lamento romántico
If only we had bought that flat in 2015 — it's worth double now.

questions.statement: 'I wish I would have known' es estándar en inglés escrito.
questions.explanation: FALSO. Aunque muchos americanos lo dicen ('I wish I woulda known'), no es estándar y te penalizarán en cualquier examen tipo Cambridge B2 First. La única forma correcta es 'I wish I HAD known'. Regla clave: nunca 'would have' después de 'wish' o 'if' condicional.
examples: Standard: I wish I had known you were vegetarian — I'd have ordered differently.
Non-standard: I wish I would have known... → aceptable oralmente en EE. UU., error escrito

questions.prompt: Empareja cada arrepentimiento con su cláusula complementaria:

pairs.left: I wish I had studied harder
If only we had left earlier,
pairs.right: we wouldn't have missed the flight.
spent so much on that car.

pairs.left: I wish I had told him
pairs.right: how much I appreciated his help.
I would have called you sooner.

questions.explanation: Todas las estructuras siguen el patrón 'wish/if only + past perfect', a menudo combinado con tercer condicional ('would have + PP') para vincular arrepentimiento con consecuencia. Es una combinación clásica en discursos reflexivos, memorias y confesiones sinceras.
examples: I wish I had listened to her advice back then — she was right all along.
If only I had known, I would have prepared something special. → cortesía cálida

questions.prompt: Un amigo te cuenta lo mal que ahorró en su veintena.
questions.question: Which sentence combines past regret with present consequence?
options: I wish I had saved more money — I'd be rich now.
I wish I save more money.
I wish I would have saved money.
I wish I saving more money.
questions.explanation: Combinación clásica de 'wish + past perfect' (arrepentimiento pasado) con 'would/could + infinitivo' (consecuencia presente). Es la misma lógica que el condicional mixto past→present, pero con marco de deseo. La marca temporal 'now' revela que el resultado sigue vivo.
examples: I wish I had studied law — I'd be earning six figures by now. → charla honesta entre amigos
I wish I had learnt to drive as a teenager. I could be so much more independent now.

questions.target: I wish I had traveled more when I was younger. Now I have too many responsibilities.
questions.explanation: Reflexión típica de adulto en los 30-40. Nota la estructura contrastiva pasado→presente que hace la frase natural. En hablado marca pausa entre las dos oraciones, y baja la entonación en 'responsibilities'. Nativos añaden hedging como 'you know', 'I guess' o 'honestly' para suavizar el tono nostálgico y no sonar quejosos.
examples: You know, I wish I had studied abroad when I had the chance. Now with the kids, it's just not realistic.
Honestly, I wish I'd learnt an instrument as a child — starting from zero at 40 is brutal.

questions.prompt: Tu amiga habla de una discusión con su hermano.
questions.question: Complete: 'She wishes she ___ that comment. It really hurt him.'
options: hasn't made
didn't make
hadn't made
wouldn't make
questions.explanation: 'Hadn't made' es la forma correcta: arrepentimiento pasado por algo que SÍ hizo (dijo un comentario hiriente). Es muy típico en reflexiones sobre discusiones o palabras dichas en caliente. Nota que en inglés decimos 'make a comment', no 'say a comment' — es una colocación fija.
examples: I wish I hadn't shouted at him in front of everyone. → arrepentimiento tras una escena
She wishes she hadn't posted that photo. It went viral for all the wrong reasons.

questions.statement: Puedes usar 'wish + past perfect' para hablar de cosas que SÍ pasaron y te alegran.
questions.explanation: FALSO. 'Wish + past perfect' SIEMPRE expresa arrepentimiento por lo que NO sucedió como querías. Para alegrarte de algo que sí pasó, usa 'I'm glad (that) I did X' o 'It was a good thing I...'. Confundirlos cambia radicalmente el significado.
examples: Regret: I wish I had gone to that concert. → realidad: no fui, ahora me pesa
Glad: I'm so glad I went to that concert — it changed my perspective on live music.

questions.text: If only I had realised how important it was, I would have paid more attention.
questions.explanation: Fórmula reflexiva típica en entrevistas o post-mortem. Weak forms: 'had' se reduce a /əd/ tras 'I' → 'I-əd realised'. 'Would have' colapsa a 'would've' /ˈwʊdəv/. Nota el énfasis en 'important' y 'more' — son las palabras emocionales que llevan el peso de la reflexión.
examples: If only I'd known then what I know now, I would've acted completely differently.
If only she had told me sooner, I would've understood the whole situation better.

questions.prompt: Redactas una nota elegante para un anfitrión que te recibió sin avisar.
questions.question: Which is the correct order in formal inversion?
options: Had I known you were coming, I would have baked a cake.
Known I had you were coming, I would have baked.
If had I known, I would have baked.
Had known I you were coming, I would have baked.
questions.explanation: Inversión formal: se elimina 'if' y se invierten 'had' + sujeto. Es equivalente a 'If I had known...' pero con registro más elevado, típico de escritura literaria, discursos y cortesía formal. Nativos también lo usan en broma cuando alguien aparece por sorpresa: 'Had I known...!'.
examples: Had I realised the meeting was in person, I would have dressed properly. → email de disculpa
Had she known the true cost, she would have negotiated much harder.

questions.target: If only I had taken that opportunity when it came up, my life would be completely different now.
questions.explanation: Combina 'if only + past perfect' con condicional mixto past→present. Es la fórmula reina de discursos motivacionales, entrevistas biográficas y reflexiones vitales profundas. En hablado, marca pausa reflexiva antes de 'my life' y da énfasis a 'completely different' con entonación descendente al final.
examples: You know, if only I'd said yes to that transfer to Berlin, everything would be different today.
If only I had spoken up in that meeting, things wouldn't be such a mess right now.

questions.prompt: Interpretación de una frase de un amigo con resaca.
questions.question: Choose the meaning of: 'I wish I hadn't drunk so much coffee last night.'
options: I drank a lot of coffee and now I regret it.
I didn't drink coffee but I wanted to.
I plan to stop drinking coffee.
I never drink coffee at night.
questions.explanation: 'Wish + hadn't + PP' implica que la persona SÍ realizó la acción y ahora se arrepiente de ello. La estructura funciona como un espejo invertido: la frase gramatical dice 'no', pero el hecho real dice 'sí'. Este mecanismo confunde a hispanohablantes porque en español el 'ojalá no hubiera bebido' es más transparente.
examples: I wish I hadn't eaten so much pizza — my stomach is killing me. → realidad: comí mucho
I wish I hadn't stayed up so late binging Netflix. → realidad: sí me quedé despierto
